data.narrative:
Shine Technologies, a Series E climate and energy company founded by Greg Piefer, has raised over $1.0B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 same-sector peers—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private companies including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—though narrow peer comparables prove sparse at this stage and tier.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and primary. Using the $1.0B total capital raised as a proxy baseline, application of a typical 1.4x Series E step-up multiplier yields $1.4B. The Peer-Median method is not applicable; while 9 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier datapoints yields insufficient coverage (0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier), below the 3-point minimum for reliable median calculation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.2B (low) to $1.6B (high), with a median of $1.4B. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.4x step-up multiplier for frontier-scale climate tech and the absence of contemporaneous comparable transaction data. A future round or additional peer M&A activity would substantially improve precision.
